siteTagline: Find your next road race across Southeast Asia
heroHeadline: Find your next road *race* across Southeast Asia
_entityUrlSegment_note: Kept as the singular 'race' to match the URL shape of the previous runsea.run site (/race/<slug>/), which Google has already indexed. Changing it to 'races' would 404 every indexed result.

theme._note: Exact design tokens from runsea.run's live design system (see Races/design.html) -- kept 1:1 so this instance's visual identity doesn't change from the engine rebuild. Every other config-examples/*.json theme is intentionally different, proving the token *shape* (not these specific values) is what the engine depends on.

_listicleConfig_note: minEntities is the floor below which a category x country guide isn't worth a page -- a three-item 'best of' reads as thin and drags on the domain rather than helping it. perRunLimit deliberately drips: ~27 combinations currently qualify, and publishing them in one week looks like a content dump to search engines and is more than anyone will actually proofread. 5/week clears the backlog over about five weeks while staying reviewable.

enabledFeatures._mergedReviews_note: When true, a race's review body is rendered ON its entity page and /reviews/<slug>/ becomes a redirect to it, instead of the two living as separate URLs. Reason: Google Search Console showed ~192 races each holding a /race/ AND a /reviews/ URL -- 69% of the sitemap covering half as many topics -- while crawl budget sat near zero and only 22 pages were indexed. Every 'Crawled - currently not indexed' URL was a /race/ page (thin: ~713 words of templated facts); the 1,500-word original reviews sat on URLs Google had never fetched at all. Merging puts the unique content on the URL Google already crawls and ranks, and halves the sitemap. Set false to restore two separate URLs -- no data changes either way, data/reviews/*.json is untouched.
enabledFeatures._autoPromoteDiscovered_note: When true, a newly-discovered race is published automatically: generate-summaries.js promotes it straight from draft to active once it has real content (never a placeholder). Set false to restore the human review gate (draft -> needs_review, still live, but flagged). Only brand-new drafts are affected; refresh's needs_review flags on existing races are untouched.

sourceConfig._discoveryWindowMonths_note: Rolling coverage window measured from the day each run executes, not a fixed end date -- so the directory keeps reaching a full year ahead every week instead of slowly running out of future.
sourceConfig._research_note: Web-research stage budget. researchPerRunLimit caps entities per weekly run so cost stays flat as the directory grows; researchIntervalDays is how long before an entity is looked at again (what people say about an event barely changes week to week). Soonest-dated entities are researched first.
sourceConfig._review_note: Review-article stage (scripts/generate-reviews.js). reviewPerRunLimit caps how many articles are SUCCESSFULLY written per run; entities with research material and the soonest upcoming date are chosen first, and existing reviews are never overwritten. The workflow ticks hourly but only generates when it's been >= reviewMinIntervalHours since the last published review. NOTE on the interval: the cron says hourly, but GitHub actually delivers only ~4 scheduled ticks a day on this repo (measured 2026-08-05: 6 scheduled runs across 37h, ~84% of ticks dropped). 20h is tuned against that real cadence to yield ~1 article/day -- the first tick that lands past the 20h mark wins, which in practice is 22-28h after the last one. Lower this to publish faster; raise it to slow down. A manual dispatch with slugs, or --force, bypasses the interval guard entirely.
sourceConfig.discoveryConstraints: Only include road races run primarily on paved or tarmac surfaces that offer a half marathon (21.1km) or a full marathon (42.195km) distance. A race whose longest distance is 10K or shorter is OUT OF SCOPE -- skip standalone fun runs, charity 5K/10K events and kids races entirely, even when a trusted calendar lists them. Shorter 5K/10K legs ARE wanted when they sit alongside a 21.1km or 42.195km distance at the same event. Do not include trail running events, off-road ultra-trail races, obstacle course races, or duathlons/triathlons -- if a source page mixes road races with trail or multisport events, extract only the road running ones.
sourceConfig._discoveryRequiredCategoryIds_note: Belt-and-braces for the distance rule stated in discoveryConstraints above: a candidate is only written if at least one of its core_facts.distance_km values falls inside one of these categories' matchRange (data/categories/*.json). Enforced in code because a model asked to extract every row of a calendar page will still hand back out-of-scope entries -- the same reason the rolling date window is checked twice. Stays vertical-agnostic: the ranges live in the category data, not in the script. Empty or absent disables the check.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_note: Each entry is fetched verbatim, so prefer a deep link to an actual country/calendar listing over a bare domain -- a homepage shows a few featured events, the calendar page shows the whole year. Country-specific entries exist because the original five sources skew heavily to Malaysia/Indonesia, leaving Vietnam, Thailand and the smaller markets underrepresented. worldathletics.org is deliberately absent: its calendar is client-rendered, so a plain fetch returns navigation and zero events, and its label road races already appear via AIMS.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_history_note: Verified reachable 2026-08-18 with the declared userAgent above. REMOVED that day: checkpointspot.asia and three ahotu.com/calendar/running/<country> URLs -- all returned HTTP 403 on every path including the site root, while their robots.txt explicitly allows this agent. That combination means CDN-level bot blocking, not a robots preference, and the only way past it would be to spoof a browser user agent, which this project will not do. Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines each keep two working feeds (finishers + justrunlah), so no country lost its only source. ALSO FIXED that day: the finishers Malaysia path, which had been 404ing since it was added -- their slug is 'malaysia-2', not 'malaysia' (a collision on their end), so Malaysia had been silently down to one feed. Laos added at the same time; it works and Laos coverage was thin. Re-probe with scripts/lib/http.js fetchText before adding any source, and prefer a deep link to the country calendar over a bare domain.
sourceConfig._discoveryChunking_note: A source page is read in successive chunks of discoveryChunkChars, up to discoveryMaxChunksPerSource, instead of only its first 6000 characters (scripts/lib/http.js chunkForPrompt). Measured 2026-08-20 with the declared userAgent: the old single-window read was showing the extractor 31% of justrunlah's Thailand calendar, 34% of Indonesia's, 55% of Vietnam's and 19% of the AIMS world calendar -- which is most of why Thailand (25) and Vietnam (10) were the thinnest countries in the directory while their calendars run to hundreds of events. Cost scales with chunks, so this is the knob to turn down if a run gets expensive; 8 x 6000 covers every source currently configured in full.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_render_note: Re-probed 2026-09-28 with the declared userAgent, measuring EXTRACTABLE TEXT rather than HTTP status. Every finishers.com entry returns 200 with ~200KB of HTML and ZERO text after scripts are stripped -- the whole calendar is client-rendered, so scripts/lib/http.js htmlToText hands the extractor nothing. Eight of the eighteen entries had therefore never yielded a single candidate and never could, while still counting as reachable and never tripping the source-failure alarm. They are moved to renderRequiredAggregators below: still the best source for a MANUAL pass driven by a rendering fetch (that is where the 2026-09-28 candidates came from), but pointless for this script. racexasia.com was dropped outright -- 200, but 2170 characters of pure navigation and no event rows. aims-worldrunning.org/calendar.html was dropped for a different reason: it renders fine but prints NO YEAR on any row, and two fetches of it disagreed about a date, so it cannot be used to date anything. The AIMS per-country pages replace it and are the best source now available -- they print "Sun 16 May 2027" in full. CORRECTED 2026-09-29: this note used to say only four countries had one. Every country in the region does -- 61 Malaysia, 90 Thailand, 82 Singapore, 18 Cambodia, 100 Philippines, 114 Indonesia, 123 Vietnam, 129 Myanmar, 150 Brunei, 151 Laos -- found by naming every countries/NN.html listed in aims-worldrunning.org/sitemap.xml.gz. Do not use aims-worldrunning.org/events.ics: robots.txt disallows /events. howei.com was evaluated and REJECTED despite working: its robots.txt asks Crawl-delay: 5 and requestDelayMs here is 1500, and fetching a site faster than it asks is not worth a thin Malaysian feed. INDONESIA, probed the same way 2026-09-28: indonesiamarathon.com/kalender-lari-2027 is the best 2027-specific feed found for any country (8.2k chars, 88 mentions of 2027) -- its year is in the path deliberately, since it IS the 2027 page, so add the 2028 page when it appears rather than editing this one. eventrack.id (44k), kalenderlari.net (a different site from kalenderlari.com), ruanglari.com and tias.co.id added. kalenderlari.com is kept at BOTH its root and its year-pathed 2026 page, per Alex -- the site publishes a fresh year page, so the pathed one is expected to move to 2027. kalenderlari.com/jadwal/ was checked and is byte-identical to the root, so not added twice. lelarian.com returned HTTP 402 and was rejected. lariku.info and ayolari.id are client-rendered (200, zero text) and live under renderRequiredAggregators.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_vietnam_note: Added 2026-09-29, probed with the declared userAgent and this script's own fetchText/htmlToText/isAllowed. The directory had only 12 Vietnamese races against ~50 road and trail races listed for Oct 2026-Mar 2027. ticket.irace.vn is Vietnam's main race-entry platform: its homepage prints the ~25 events currently on sale as plain text (name, date, province, price), robots.txt allows this agent, and there is no pagination, so the root IS the listing. irace.vn/su-kien and irace.vn/ are client-rendered (1-3k chars of navigation) and must not be used. linh.academy/kien-thuc/giai-chay/giai-chay-bo is a Vietnamese running coach's calendar of ~50 races (54k chars of text), re-checked monthly against each official site; it corrects dates the aggregators get wrong (VPBank Hanoi 18 Oct not 25 Oct; Tien Phong Marathon 20-21 Mar 2027 not 28 Mar), so treat it as the better date source when the two disagree. Both list trail races and 5K/10K fun runs: discoveryConstraints and discoveryRequiredCategoryIds already keep those out.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_2026_09_29_sweep_not: Region-wide source sweep 2026-09-29, run because Alex had handed over two Vietnamese sources we had never found, which meant the earlier search was not comprehensive. Every market was searched in English and its own language across entry platforms, calendar blogs, coaches and clubs, federations, timing firms and tourism boards; about 190 candidates were probed with scripts/lib/http.js and the declared userAgent, and each was judged by how many in-window 21.1/42.2 km road races it listed that the directory lacked. Measured gaps: Thailand 82, Philippines 45, Malaysia 28, Indonesia 13, Vietnam 12, Cambodia/Laos 2, Singapore/Brunei 0 (Singapore's thin count is a calendar fact; Brunei has three recurring halves with no date yet). REMOVED: justrunlah's Philippines (newest row Nov 2025), Thailand (Dec 2025), Indonesia (Nov 2023) and Malaysia (nothing after Sep 2026) calendars -- all return 200 with rows, so they never tripped a failure alarm, but they had stopped updating. Its Singapore and Vietnam pages still carry in-window rows and are kept. ADDED, all plain text, robots allow, no Crawl-delay: AIMS pages for the six countries previously thought to have none. MALAYSIA: lesgo.my filtered to half and full marathon (21 of the 28 missing races; page 2 of the half filter carries the 2027 rows), Pacemakers Malaysia's blog calendar pm1.blogspot.com (dates but no distances; its path says 2026 but it runs Sep 2026-Aug 2027), and JomRun's state pages for Sabah 10, Sarawak 11, Selangor 12, Terengganu 13 and Johor 14 -- the plain jomrun.com/events page shows only featured fun runs, and the other states' pages held no half marathon when checked, so add them if that changes. PHILIPPINES: pinoyfitness.com's calendar (organiser-submitted like iRace, 144 events to Aug 2027, 26.8k chars, no pagination; /list-of-events/ is the same page) and runrio.com/race-calendar (only RunRio's own races, but its distances are authoritative: Pinoy Fitness listed EastWest Dream Run CDO as 12K max, RunRio says 21K). THAILAND: runlah.com (a Thai race-entry platform, ~80 in-window races, but only to about Feb 2027, mixes in trail races and mis-tags distances -- it tagged the 2.5/5/10K Thailand Post EMS RUN as a full marathon), thesublist.run's half and marathon pages (road only, exact dates), regis.run and worldsmarathons.com/c/marathon/thailand (the only plain sources reaching May-Jun 2027). Thai sources use Buddhist Era: 2570 BE = 2027. SINGAPORE: catalystperformance.sg's 2027 page, a coaching studio that updates each race as its 2027 date is confirmed -- add the 2028 page when it appears rather than editing this one. VIETNAM: pace8.vn/su-kien pages 1-2 (an entry platform separate from iRace; every row has year, date range, distances and a ROAD/TRAIL label) and bestmarathon.vn/race-info (weaker dates: some provisional, and it had VPBank Hanoi on 25 Oct -- linh.academy wins when they disagree). REJECTED: takbo.ph (Crawl-delay 50), runph.org (30), gotorace (20), chiptimethailand (10), raceroster (5), racetime.sg and the Brunei organiser sites (long crawl delays); ahotu, raceyaya.com, tourismthailand.org (403); 5BIB (no year or distances, dates a day or two early); pew.vn (a 2026 list re-labelled 2027, so no date on it can be trusted); race|result's event list (robots disallows). ayolari.id now serves plain text (675 events) and was taken off renderRequiredAggregators, but it is not added: it listed no race the Indonesian feeds above lack, and no 2027 rows. The configured indonesiamarathon.com/kalender-lari-2027 page only prints its first 18 rows as text; the rest load by script -- see manualPassSources.
sourceConfig._manualPassSources_note: Sources discover-entities.js does NOT read, for a manual pass. They are either JSON or render-only, and unlike renderRequiredAggregators some are the best feed for their country. dasbor.indonesiamarathon.com's API is the JSON behind indonesiamarathon.com and schedules.run, which pools schedules.run, kalenderlari.net, jadwallari and kalenderlari.com: 361 half-marathon and 202 marathon rows with ISO event_date and event_type (road-run / trail-run / fun-run / virtual-run), 50 a page, paged with &page=N. It ignores date and type filters and returns past events too, so filter locally on event_type road-run and event_date inside the window. schedules.run/YYYY/MM is the same data as a page (rows sit in the script data-page=app JSON at props.schedules.data), so use one or the other, not both. race.thai.run is Thailand's national entry platform but client-rendered; idorunubon.github.io/events.json is a weekly JSON copy of it that added nothing beyond runlah.com when checked. ewent.la is the Lao ticketing platform (render-only). worldsmarathons.com/marathon/pakse-half-marathon's similar-events block is the best view of the Lao road calendar.
sourceConfig._renderRequiredAggregators_note: Client-rendered calendars. A plain fetch returns 200 and no text, so discover-entities.js does NOT read this key and must not be pointed at them. They are kept because they are the widest SEA listing available to a manual pass using a rendering fetch, and because deleting them would lose the knowledge that they exist and what they are good for. They list roughly fifteen 2027 races for the region, but at month precision once an event is more than a few months out ("Early May 2027"), so treat them as a source of CANDIDATES and never of dates.

notes: Vertical instance config for 'races' (runsea.run). This file is the ONLY place vertical labels/branding/behavior are read from by shared engine code -- no vertical-specific strings should ever be hardcoded into /src or /scripts. See /config-examples for how the other four verticals (hotels, local-services, courses, event-planning) instantiate the same schema. Do NOT point DNS/CNAME at runsea.run's live production traffic until this engine's races vertical has passed Step 5 review and a manual QA pass.
